info.name: Sentinel API
info.description:
Sentinel Backend â€” Express + Drizzle.

Grows one folder per module: `Auth`, `Users`, `Vendors`, `Transactions`. The Sprint 2 AI service (`/analyze`, `/chat`) lives in a separate repo and collection.

## Setup
1. Import `sentinel_local.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Seed a Finance Lead: `npm run db:seed -- lead@company.com "Nama"`.
3. Put that email and password into the `seedEmail` / `seedPassword` variables.
4. Run **Auth â†’ Login (password)**. It captures `accessToken` and `refreshToken` automatically â€” every other request reuses them, so no copy-pasting.

## Order that works end to end
Login â†’ Users: Create member (captures `memberId` + `tempPassword`) â†’ Users: List â†’ Users: Deactivate member.

Separately: Login â†’ Vendors: Create Vendor (captures `vendorId`) â†’ Transactions: Create Transaction (B2B Sales) (spends `vendorId`, captures `transactionId`) â†’ Transactions: List / Get / Update.

`Guards` holds the negative cases. They are meant to fail with a specific status, and their tests assert exactly that â€” a green run there means the API is refusing what it should.

item.name: Vendors
item.description: Companies on the other side of a transaction â€” a supplier being paid, or (for `B2B Sales`) the buyer. No Delete endpoint: a vendor is retired by setting `status: "inactive"`, same pattern as Users.

request.description: `status` defaults to `active` when omitted. Captures `vendorId`, spent by Transactions â†’ Create Transaction (B2B Sales).
Partial update â€” only sent fields change. Setting `status: "inactive"` is how a vendor is retired; there is no delete endpoint.
